meta.notes: Original NMAT-style practice items. These are not actual or reconstructed NMAT questions. The set uses the three Perceptual Acuity item types documented by CEM: Hidden Figure, Mirror Image, and Identical Information. Practice distribution: 10 items per type. Answer keys are distributed across A-E to avoid a predictable pattern.
validationNotes: Hidden Figure uses a simple target plus five complicated drawings.
Mirror Image uses one asymmetric figure plus five visual options.
Identical Information uses a sentence, biographical entry, or bibliographical entry and tests exact matching of spelling, punctuation, and word sequence.

The official NMAT documentation identifies 40 Perceptual Acuity items with a 40-minute recommended time allotment in the published NMAT bulletin; this 30-item set is a practice set, not an official simulation length.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- a four-sided shape with a flat top edge, a short diagonal edge down to a sharp right-pointing vertex, a long diagonal edge down to a sharp bottom vertex, and a concave arc closing it back to the top-left corner -- is embedded in Drawing C near the upper-center of the circle. It appears in essentially the same orientation as the simple figure, merely shifted to a different position within the circle, with its exact proportions preserved. The other drawings contain similarly styled lines and curves, but none reproduces the target's specific vertex angles, edge lengths, and arc curvature together as a single closed region.
questions.hint: Lock onto the one curved (concave) edge of the target and the sharp point directly opposite it -- this pairing is the most distinctive feature to scan for inside each circle, since most distractor lines in this item are straight.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- an elongated, boot-shaped outline with several gently bending straight edges along its left side, a short notch near the top, a sharp inner vertex, a pointed lower-right corner, and a small curved (hooked) edge near its opposite end -- is traced by the leftmost diagonal, the near-vertical line, and the small curved hook inside Drawing A, rotated roughly 155-160 degrees from its original orientation. Every edge of the target lines up with an actual drawn line in Drawing A, including the distinctive curved hook near the bottom. In Drawings B, C, D, and E, at least part of the same outline either falls on blank space or only appears to match by tracing the diamond-and-circle frame that is common to all five drawings, rather than the unique lines specific to that option.
questions.hint: All five drawings share the same outer hourglass-and-diamond frame, so ignore that outline entirely -- it's common to every option and can't help you. Focus only on the internal lines unique to each drawing, and look for the one small curved (hooked) segment paired with a long, gently bending straight edge running most of the figure's length.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- an arrow-like polygon with a pointed top, a short inward notch on its left side, and a long, narrow blade tapering to a sharp point below -- is traced almost exactly by lines in the upper portion of Drawing A, appearing in nearly its original orientation (barely rotated) and merely shifted to a different spot within the circle. Every edge and vertex of the target lines up with an actual drawn line in Drawing A. Drawings B, C, D, and E contain similarly angled lines and triangular clusters, but none reproduces the target's specific notch position, edge lengths, and closing angle together as one continuous outline -- their nearest candidate shapes leave at least one edge crossing blank space.
questions.hint: Notice the small inward step on the target's left side, partway down from the top point. Search each drawing for a slender, dagger-like cluster of lines near the rim of the circle, then check whether that same small step-in appears at the matching spot before locking in your answer.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- a narrow, elongated five-sided shape resembling a tag or ticket, with one corner chamfered off at the top -- is traced with near-pixel precision by lines in the upper-left portion of Drawing B, rotated roughly 140 degrees from its original orientation. Every edge and vertex, including the short chamfered corner, aligns exactly with an actual drawn line in Drawing B. Drawings A, C, D, and E contain similarly dense crisscrossing lines within their ovals, but none reproduces the target's specific proportions, chamfer angle, and vertex sequence as a single continuous outline.
questions.hint: The target is a slim, elongated shape with one corner sliced off at an angle -- almost like a fence post with a pointed cap. Look for a tall, narrow quadrilateral-ish outline near the edge of each oval, then check whether one of its top corners is cut at that same shallow angle.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- a five-sided shape with a long top edge, a straight right side, an inward-pointing notch partway down, and a sharp point at the bottom -- is traced with near-pixel precision by lines in Drawing B, rotated approximately 90 degrees clockwise from its original orientation. Every edge, including the distinctive inward notch, aligns almost exactly with an actual drawn line in Drawing B. Drawings A, C, D, and E contain similarly crossing diagonal lines within their squares, but none reproduces the target's specific notch position, edge lengths, and closing point together as one continuous outline.
questions.hint: The target's most distinctive feature is the inward notch partway down its right side, right before the shape narrows to a sharp bottom point. Look for that same 'step-in then taper to a point' pattern among each square's crossing lines before settling on an answer.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- a crown-like shape with two sharp peaks, a slightly curved (convex) right edge, a straight bottom edge, and an internal diagonal line running from the bottom-left corner up to the valley between the two peaks -- is traced almost exactly by lines in the lower portion of Drawing D, appearing in essentially its original orientation (unrotated), just shifted lower within the frame. Every edge, including the internal diagonal and both peaks, aligns almost exactly with an actual drawn line in Drawing D. Drawings A, B, C, and E contain similarly angled crossing lines within their wavy-sided frames, but none reproduces the target's specific peak spacing, curve, and internal diagonal together as one continuous figure.
questions.hint: The target has a unique internal line cutting across it diagonally, in addition to its two-peaked outline. Look for a two-pointed 'crown' shape with a diagonal line slicing through its middle in each drawing, rather than just matching the outer silhouette alone.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- a crown- or star-topped shape with a left point, a center peak, and a right point, narrowing below into a straight-sided ribbon that ends in an angled bottom edge -- is traced by lines running from the upper-left through the center of Drawing C, rotated roughly 285 degrees from its original orientation. The double-peaked star top and the long ribbon edge extending to the right both align closely with actual drawn lines in Drawing C. Drawings A, B, D, and E contain similar zigzag, star-like clusters of lines, but each leaves at least one segment of the target's outline crossing blank space rather than tracing a real line.
questions.hint: Look for the small double-notch 'crown' silhouette (a left point, then a center peak, then a right point) attached to a long straight-edged tail. Trace the whole outline continuously rather than just spotting the crown shape alone, since a few drawings show a similar-looking crown without the matching tail.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- an elongated, gently angled shape with a notched upper-left edge and a wider, straight-edged base -- is traced with pixel-level precision by lines in the upper petal of Drawing A, appearing in essentially its original orientation (unrotated), just repositioned within the pinwheel-shaped frame. Every edge and vertex of the target lines up almost exactly with an actual drawn line in Drawing A. Drawings B, C, D, and E contain similarly dense crisscrossing lines within their petals, but none reproduces the target's specific notch position, edge lengths, and vertex sequence as one continuous outline.
questions.hint: All five drawings share the same four-petal pinwheel outline, so focus only on the internal lines inside each petal. Look for the small notch near the top of the target and a wide, straight-edged base directly beneath it, within a single petal of the figure.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- a wide, sail- or leaf-shaped figure with two straight edges meeting at a sharp point on one side and a gently curved edge closing it on the other -- is traced with near-pixel precision by lines in the center-left of Drawing C, rotated roughly 168 degrees from its original orientation. Both straight edges and the curved base align almost exactly with actual drawn lines in Drawing C. Drawings A, B, D, and E contain similarly angled lines and curves within their squares, but none reproduces the target's specific proportions and curvature together as one continuous outline.
questions.hint: The target has two straight sides meeting at a sharp point and one gently curved side opposite them. Look for a wide, shallow triangle-like shape with one curved edge in each drawing, paying attention to how gently that one edge bows compared to the two straight sides.

questions.prompt: Which complicated drawing contains the simple target figure?
questions.explanation: The target figure -- an irregular arrowhead-like shape with a notched top edge, a long straight right side tapering to a point, and a narrow rectangular foot at the bottom -- is traced with pixel-level precision by lines in the center of Drawing B, rotated exactly 90 degrees from its original orientation. Every edge and vertex of the target lines up almost exactly with an actual drawn line in Drawing B. Drawings A, C, D, and E contain similarly dense triangular clusters of lines within their circles, but none reproduces the target's specific notch, proportions, and vertex sequence as one continuous outline.
questions.hint: The target's most distinctive feature is the small notch near its top edge, paired with a narrow rectangular 'foot' at the opposite end. Look for that same notch-plus-foot combination among each circle's crossing lines, keeping in mind the whole figure may be rotated a quarter turn from how it's shown at the left.
